chunks.title: Product Specifications
chunks.content: Coway Airmega Mighty / AP-1512HH air purifier covers up to 1,748 ft² (162 m²) at 60 min ACPH, CADR 233 (Smoke), 3-stage airflow, 8-hour timer, 120V~60Hz, 77W, 16.8x18.3x9.6 in, 12.3 lbs.

chunks.title: Power Cord and Electrical Danger
chunks.content: Never operate with a damaged plug/cord; use a dedicated grounded 120V/60Hz outlet; disconnect if strange sounds, smells, or smoke occur and contact service immediately.

scenarios.condition: Strange sounds, smells, or smoke come from the product
steps: Disconnect the power plug from the electric outlet immediately
Contact the customer service center for instructions

scenarios.condition: Power plug or cord is damaged
steps: Do not attempt to repair the cord yourself
Contact a service center to replace it

chunks.title: Fire and Combustible Material Hazards
chunks.content: Do not place near flammable gases, cigarettes, incense, combustibles; never spray insecticides or flammable materials near or into the air inlet.

scenarios.condition: Product is near flammable materials or sprays
steps: Never place unit near flammable gases, cigarettes, incense, or combustibles
Never spray insecticides or air fresheners near or into the air inlet

chunks.title: Child Safety and Openings Warning
chunks.content: Not for use by children under 8 or those with reduced capabilities without supervision; do not insert objects/fingers into openings; do not let children climb or hang on the unit.

chunks.title: Polarized Plug and Damaged Cord Warning
chunks.content: This appliance has a polarized plug that fits an outlet only one way; do not defeat this safety feature, and never operate a fan with a damaged cord or plug.

chunks.title: Placement and Clearance Cautions
chunks.content: Do not install on a sloped surface; keep at least 20 cm from walls/objects and 30-60 cm clearance above; keep 2 m away from electronics like TVs; avoid direct sunlight.

chunks.title: Ozone Emission Compliance
chunks.content: Product complies with max ozone concentration of 0.050 ppmv over 24 hours, per Health Canada Guideline 2010 recommendations.

chunks.title: Parts Overview and Air Quality Indicator
chunks.content: The unit has a front cover, air quality sensor, operation/indication panel, handle, air outlet, and power cord; the round lamp glows blue (clean), dark purple (polluted), or red (highly polluted).

chunks.title: Filter Installation
chunks.content: Open the front cover by pulling the top, remove plastic packaging from each filter, and install in order: HEPA filter, then Deodorization filter, then Pre-filter, pushing the grip firmly to seat the pre-filter.

chunks.title: Operating Modes: Manual, Auto, Eco
chunks.content: Press the power button then the speed button to cycle Auto→1→2→3→ECO; Auto mode optimizes speed 1-3 based on the dust sensor, and Eco mode stops the fan after 30 minutes of no detected pollution to save energy.

chunks.title: Ionizer and Timer Controls
chunks.content: Press the Ionizer button to toggle the ionizer on/off, and hold it 3 seconds to turn the air quality indicating light on/off; press the Timer button to cycle 1H→4H→8H→off, holding to deactivate.

chunks.title: Adjust Air Quality Sensor Sensitivity
chunks.content: While powered on, press and hold the airflow speed and ionizer buttons for 2 seconds to enter sensitivity mode, then press the speed button to select Sensitive/Standard/Insensitive, and hold both buttons again for 2 seconds (or wait 10 seconds) to confirm.

chunks.title: Cleaning the Air Quality Sensor
chunks.content: Every 2 months, open the air quality sensor cover on the right side, clean the air inlet/outlet vent and sensor with a soft brush or vacuum, then lightly moisten a cotton swab to clean the lens, dust inlet, and dust outlet, finishing with a dry swab.

chunks.title: Cleaning Air Inlet, Outlet, Front Cover, and Body
chunks.content: Clean the air inlet/outlet with a soft brush every 2 months; wipe the front cover and product body with a dry soft cloth (or lightly damp cloth for tough dirt) every 2-4 weeks; never use detergents, thinners, bleach, or abrasives, and never submerge or spray water directly on the unit.

chunks.title: Cleaning the Pre-Filter
chunks.content: Every 2-4 weeks, open the front cover, press down the top clip of the pre-filter and pull it out carefully, clean with a vacuum or water depending on contamination level, then dry completely before reinstalling and fitting it into the hooks correctly.

chunks.title: Filter Replacement Cycles and Indicator Reset
chunks.content: Pre-filter is cleaned every 2-4 weeks; Deodorization filter replaced every 6 months; HEPA filter replaced every 1 year (based on 8-hour max-speed use); after replacing, hold the Reset button 2 seconds to clear the indicator, or use forcible reset mode to reset a filter early.

chunks.title: Air Purifier Troubleshooting Guide
chunks.content: Covers no airflow, unchanging speed, weak airflow, bad smell, and stuck pollution indicator issues with checks and fixes before contacting service.

tasks.title: Install Filters Before First Use
tasks.description: Unpack and install the HEPA, deodorization, and pre-filter in the correct order before first running the purifier.
tasks.justification: Running the unit without filters removed from packaging or in the wrong order reduces filtration performance.
tasks.instructions_text: Open the front cover by pulling the top. Remove the plastic packaging from each filter. Install them in this order: HEPA filter first, then the deodorization filter, then the pre-filter, pushing the grip until it clicks firmly into place.

tasks.title: Connect to Dedicated Grounded Outlet
tasks.description: Verify the unit is plugged into a dedicated grounded 120V/60Hz electrical outlet not shared with other devices.
tasks.justification: Using an ungrounded outlet or shared power strip risks electric shock or fire.
tasks.instructions_text: Plug the power cord directly into a grounded 120V, 60Hz wall outlet dedicated to this product. Do not use a power strip shared with other appliances.

re_check_triggers.description: Burning smell, sparks, or shock when touching the unit

tasks.title: Verify Placement Clearances
tasks.description: Position the purifier away from slopes, walls, sunlight, and electronics with the recommended clearances.
tasks.justification: Blocked airflow or improper placement reduces cleaning efficiency and can affect nearby electronics.
tasks.instructions_text: Place the unit on a flat, level surface with at least 20 cm clearance from walls/objects and 30-60 cm clearance above it. Keep it at least 2 m from TVs or other electronics and out of direct sunlight.

re_check_triggers.description: Unit seems to clean air slower than expected or airflow feels blocked

tasks.title: Clean the Pre-Filter
tasks.description: Remove and clean the reusable pre-filter with a vacuum or water depending on contamination level.
tasks.justification: A dirty pre-filter reduces airflow and overall product performance and shortens the life of the deodorization and HEPA filters behind it.
tasks.instructions_text: Open the front cover, press the top clip of the pre-filter and pull it out carefully to avoid dropping dust. Clean it with a vacuum cleaner, or wash with water if heavily soiled, then let it dry completely before reinstalling and fitting it into the hooks correctly.

tasks.title: Replace the Deodorization Filter
tasks.description: Replace the deodorization filter approximately every 6 months.
tasks.justification: An expired deodorization filter no longer removes odors and can let bad smells return through the air outlet.
tasks.instructions_text: Unplug the unit, open the front cover, remove the old deodorization filter and packaging from the new one, and install it in the correct order (HEPA, then deodorization, then pre-filter). After replacing, hold the Reset button for 2 seconds to clear the indicator.

tasks.title: Replace the HEPA Filter
tasks.description: Replace the HEPA filter approximately once a year.
tasks.justification: An expired HEPA filter loses its ability to trap fine particles, reducing air cleaning performance.
tasks.instructions_text: Unplug the unit, open the front cover, remove the old HEPA filter, and install the new one first in the stacking order (HEPA, then deodorization, then pre-filter). After replacing, press the Reset button for 2 seconds to clear the filter indicator.

tasks.title: Clean the Air Quality Sensor
tasks.description: Clean the air quality sensor's inlet, outlet vent, and lens every 2 months.
tasks.justification: Dust buildup on the sensor lens causes the pollution indicator to stop responding accurately, so the unit may run at the wrong fan speed.
tasks.instructions_text: Open the air quality sensor cover on the right side of the unit. Use a soft brush or vacuum to clean the air inlet/outlet vent and sensor. Lightly moisten a cotton swab to clean the lens, dust inlet, and dust outlet, then use a dry swab to remove remaining moisture.

tasks.title: Clean the Air Inlet and Outlet Vents
tasks.description: Brush dust off the air inlet and outlet vents every 2 months.
tasks.justification: Accumulated dust on the vents restricts airflow and reduces purifier efficiency.
tasks.instructions_text: Use a soft brush to clean the air inlet and outlet vents, taking care not to let dust fall inside the unit. If heavily covered in dust, run the purifier in manual mode for 10 minutes to blow the dust off the vents before resuming normal use.

tasks.title: Clean the Front Cover and Body
tasks.description: Wipe the front cover and exterior body with a dry or lightly damp cloth every 2-4 weeks.
tasks.justification: Cosmetic only — keeps dust and surface grime off the exterior and front cover.
tasks.instructions_text: Separate the front cover from the unit and wipe dust off with a soft dry brush or cloth. Wipe the product body with a dry soft cloth, using a lightly dampened cloth only for tougher dirt.
